material_issues.issue: The Redis fast-path key idem:resp:{idempotency_key} has no merchant scope and no request-hash check. This contradicts P3 and FR-5 and causes cross-tenant collisions, because order IDs are accepted as keys.
The Fraud Hook detokenises the PAN using the Card Adapter's role and sends it to FRV-1, yet the §12.2 scope table lists the Fraud Hook as out of CDE scope. This contradicts P2 and NFR-5.

Keeping the CVC until settlement or for up to 72 hours, including for incremental authorizations, conflicts with the PCI DSS v4.x ban on storing SAD after authorization (Req 3.3.1). The design misreads 3.2.1/3.3.2.

Zero-RPO NFR-4 is impossible with asynchronous Aurora Global replication. The idempotency rebuild from the payment table is impossible because the table has no key column, and the 30-minute RTO exceeds the NFR-3 monthly budget.
The latency budget assumes fewer than 1% of payments cascade, but the baseline gives 3.8% retryable outcomes, and the 2,500 ms timeout alone exceeds the 1,500 ms NFR-2 limit.
Reconciliation waits for all files. ACQ-TH1 arrives at 06:30 ICT (07:30 SGT), and matching plus reporting adds 60 minutes, giving about 08:30 SGT and missing the NFR-8 08:00 deadline.
A single CloudHSM in one AZ, with a 1,500 TPS trigger for adding a second that is never reached (55% of 2,000 = 1,100), is a single point of failure for card payments. The CDE also has no DR path.

The DynamoDB per-partition limit is misstated (AWS documents 1,000 WCU/s, not 10,000), and the WCU calculation ignores item size and LSI writes. The largest merchant's single partition key will throttle.

sound_areas.area: Double-entry ledger committed in the same transaction with an outbox, append-only enforced by revoked DML, nightly recomputation, and balanced examples
Integer minor-unit money representation with an ISO 4217 exponent table and adapters that reject rounding
Webhook signing, bounded retry schedule, per-endpoint isolation and SSRF protection

verdict_extracted.text: label not_fit, confidence 0.75: 'As written, the design is not fit to build. The core architecture is sound.' Gives a per-objective breakdown and a 'what_would_change_it' list.
verdict_extracted.label: not_fit

D1.justification: The intent summary accurately covers purpose, scope, the volume targets, P1-P10, the key FRs and NFRs, and the constraints, all cited to p.1-3. A decision registry keeps approved decisions (§24), pending backlog items (§25) and constraints apart. Findings are judged against the design's own principles and NFRs, not generic practice. Self-acknowledged gaps are credited: FND-026 cites Backlog item 2 and adds that the §27 and §28 readiness tables are inconsistent with it. Every challenge to a confirmed decision is backed by the design's own text.
review_quotes: MPOP is Serindit Pay's Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform... replaces five per-market integration stacks with one merchant API
The backlog acknowledges the item; this finding points out that the readiness and phase tables do not reflect it.
Principles take precedence: where a later section conflicts with a principle, the principle wins.

D2.justification: The verdict is explicit (not_fit), with confidence 0.75 and a breakdown across 18 objectives, principles and NFRs, each tied to finding IDs. 'what_would_change_it' lists the concrete conditions, each linked to a finding, for moving to fit_with_conditions, and the evidence that would move it further toward not_fit. The verdict follows from 1 critical and 11 high findings and separates the document from the architecture ('reflects the document as it stands'). The empty 'conditions' array is a formatting gap only; the conditions are given in what_would_change_it.
review_quotes: As written, the design is not fit to build. The core architecture is sound.
The verdict would move to fit_with_conditions if a revised design did the following
The verdict does not depend on any of these unverified findings.

D3.justification: All six categories are covered with anchored, material items: strengths (FND-058, FND-014, sound areas), risks (FND-001, 046, 049, 048, 047, 018, 054), gaps (FND-030, FND-052, FND-057), ambiguity (FND-029), unresolved assumptions (FND-026, FND-043) and validation needs (FND-027, FND-034). Every issue in my pre-read is covered, two of them only partially because they are hedged (CVC/PCI, DynamoDB limits). The review also finds valid issues I had not listed: the go-live sequencing contradiction, duplicate authorizations from timeout cascades, payout-account takeover, and state-machine gaps. There is no padding.
review_quotes: Redis idempotency fast path keyed without merchant or body hash
Go-live comes before fraud scoring, PCI assessment and load/DR validation
Cascading after a timeout or 5xx can leave duplicate live authorizations; late approvals are discarded

D4.justification: Every finding has page, section and verbatim quote anchors, and the harness verified all of them. The evidence register separates doc quotes from derived inferences. However, two material external claims have no source. The PCI DSS rule on CVC retention and the DynamoDB per-partition limit both rest on 'the reviewer's understanding'. Both are correct in substance and properly hedged, but neither cites an authoritative source. No hallucinations were found.
review_quotes: As the reviewer understands PCI DSS, card verification codes may not be kept once authorization is complete
The per-partition figure is far above the reviewer's understanding of DynamoDB's documented limit and must be checked.
D4.anchor_tension: Location traceability is at level 4, but unsourced external claims on two material points rule out 4.

D5.justification: Every material recommendation states the issue, rationale, supporting evidence IDs, expected benefit, objective references, and a concrete verification step. The elements fit together and are specific and bounded. FND-001 gives the exact new key schema and tests. FND-047 splits definite from ambiguous outcomes and adds a simulator case with an approval at 2,600 ms. FND-018 offers three bounded options.
review_quotes: change the Redis key to idem:resp:{merchant_id}:{idempotency_key}. Store request_hash with the cached response and compare it on every hit
Pass if a reversal is sent for attempt 1 and exactly one authorization stays live at the simulator.
cut the per-attempt timeout and set a total cascade deadline that fits within 1,500 ms

D6.justification: The review affirms the ledger, money representation, webhooks, back-office controls and Aurora capacity, with reasons. Each challenge to a confirmed decision (one HSM, MFA optional, batch reconciliation, go-live gate) cites the design's own evidence. FND-034 makes its schema change conditional on investigation. Severity is not always calibrated. FND-022 is rated high, but its REQUIRES_ACTION->FAILED claim is overstated, because REQUIRES_ACTION->AUTHORISING->FAILED is permitted. FND-046, which undermines PCI scope, is arguably understated at high.
review_quotes: The design meets FR-10 and P5 through database-enforced mechanisms rather than convention... so no change is justified.
The key or LSI change is conditional on the investigation showing that DynamoDB limits bind
D6.anchor_tension: Strong restraint overall, but one severity is inflated and one is understated, which fits anchor 3 better than 4.

D7.justification: Every finding has a primary disposition (refinement_now, needs_investigation, needs_testing, governance_decision) and secondary labels where the item is mixed. The labels are mostly correct; for example, the RPO restatement is governance and the CVC question is investigation with a QSA. Every non-refinement item names an owner and a phase-timed next step. The unresolved items are consolidated in one list. Some pure refinements (FND-047, FND-054, FND-052) have no owner, but the anchor does not require one for refinements.
review_quotes: Decide the RPO restatement or the synchronous design, and approve the payment schema change before Phase 3.
owner: PCI DSS compliance lead with the QSA
Choose option (a) or (b) and agree the CDE scope with the QSA before Phase 2

D8.justification: No external research was done, although the design depends on several externally checkable matters: PCI DSS SAD rules, DynamoDB partition and LSI limits, CloudHSM multi-AZ guidance, and SEA payment regulation. The review says plainly that this was caused by a tool failure, records what remains uncertain, and routes the dependent findings to investigation with owners. That calibrated deferral keeps the score above 0, but it does not replace the research. Two checkable questions (DynamoDB at 1,000 WCU, PCI DSS Req 3.3.1) were left hedged when a lookup would have settled them.
review_quotes: No external research was possible (DEG-002), so the premises behind FND-032... and FND-034... rest on the reviewer's understanding and are unverified
Whether any such constraint applies is unverified
D8.anchor_tension: Between 1 and 2. The absence of research where it was clearly needed matches anchor 1; transparency lifts it above 0 but not to 2.

D9.justification: All outputs are present, the severity counts in the verdict match the findings (1 critical, 11 high), and the quotes were verified. There are several internal inconsistencies, though. FND-014 refers to a nonexistent FND-002. SA-009 refers to nonexistent FND-004 and FND-013. The limitations say FND-049 reverses AD-006 and FND-029 reverses AD-012, which contradicts those findings' own 'preserves'/'refines' labels. The verdict's 'conditions' array is empty. FND-022 partly overstates the gap in the state machine.
review_quotes: turns contradictions such as FND-001 and FND-002 into build ambiguity
The exceptions are covered in FND-004, FND-013 and FND-014.
FND-049's recommendation appears to reverse approved decision AD-006 (24 Idempotency store) without a 'challenges' label.
D9.anchor_tension: Each inconsistency is minor, but there are several, so anchor 2 applies rather than 3.

D10.justification: The review is well structured: intent, verdict with breakdown, ranked findings, recommendations, unresolved list, decision registry and limitations, in a neutral tone. The sound_areas section is padded with near-duplicates. The ledger is affirmed four times (SA-001, 006, 012, 015), webhooks four times (SA-003, 008, 011, 013), money twice, back-office twice and Aurora twice. Auto-generated limitation notes that contradict the findings make it harder to follow.
review_quotes: Same-transaction journals with an outbox, append-only enforced by revoked DML rights
The ledger invariants, same-transaction journaling and balance projection meet FR-10 and P1/P5

top_strengths: It finds the core material defects from the document's own text, with verified quotes: idempotency key scoping, Fraud Hook PAN outside the CDE, async RPO, the cascade latency contradiction, the reconciliation deadline arithmetic, and the single HSM.

Every verdict and challenge to a confirmed decision is backed by the design's own evidence. Each challenge is labelled, and the verdict has a per-objective breakdown with explicit change conditions and confidence.
Triage is precise: governance and investigation items have named owners and next steps tied to build phases, and they are consolidated in one unresolved list.
top_improvements: Research the externally checkable premises: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 3.3.1 on SAD after authorization, AWS DynamoDB per-partition (1,000 WCU) and LSI 10 GB limits, and CloudHSM multi-AZ guidance. Cite these sources so hedged findings become definite.
Fix the internal consistency problems: the dangling finding IDs (FND-002, FND-004, FND-013), and the limitation notes that contradict the findings' own decision-relation labels.
Deduplicate sound_areas, and calibrate FND-022's severity: the REQUIRES_ACTION->FAILED gap is partly answered by the REQUIRES_ACTION->AUTHORISING->FAILED path.
uncertainty_notes: Key-blind mode, so coverage was judged against my own pre-read. The D8 score of 1 penalises the absence of research even though the review discloses the tool failure. A grader who gives more weight to that transparency might award 2. The D9 score of 2 rests on an accumulation of minor inconsistencies, none of which is material. The review was complete and not truncated.
